claims.claim: Amphilochius of Iconium was a Christian bishop of the fourth century, born ca. 339/340, probably at Caesarea in Cappadocia, and died probably between 394 and 403.
Amphilochius became bishop of Iconium early in 374, probably placed there by Basil of Caesarea.

Amphilochius was a first cousin of Gregory of Nazianzus and was brought up in the Christian aristocracy of Cappadocia; he studied for the bar and practiced at Constantinople before retiring to lead a religious life.
The homily In Zacchaeum (Homily VIII) is one of Amphilochius's genuine extant Greek homilies, edited by Cornelis Datema in Corpus Christianorum, Series Graeca 3 (1978).
Amphilochius's homily on Zacchaeus is characterized by elaborate narrative and characterization, similar to his elaboration of the sinful woman in Homily IV.

According to the opening line of Homily IV (On the Sinful Woman), Amphilochius wrote a homily on Zacchaeus that was well-known to his audience, though Datema doubts whether the extant Homily VIII is the one envisaged there, suggesting instead that it may have been preached at Caesarea as a guest of Basil rather than at Iconium.
